topic: Entry 13: x^n = f(n) := n F_{-1}(n) where x = a log x, |a|>=e (Lambert-W / Lagrange-inversion result)
note: This is essentially Lagrange's celebrated 'Lagrange inversion formula' applied to x = a log x. The key move: f(n) = f(1)^n = x^n where x solves a functional equation x = a log x. This is FRACTIONAL FUNCTIONAL ITERATION territory: an analytic function defined implicitly through a fixed-point equation, extended to all real (and complex) n by analytic continuation of the integer iterate. Berndt: 'Entries 13 and 14 have a long history. Entry 14 was first established by Lambert [1, pp. 38-40] in a paper published in 1758. In 1770, Lagrange [1] published a proof of the celebrated Lagrange inversion formula. As an application, he derived Entry 14.' The 'Schroder/Koenig fractional iteration' from the diary-20 operator definition includes Lagrange-inversion-style implicitly defined solutions of functional equations.

topic: §9 Ramanujan's 'ingenious formal technique': f(x^n) -> phi(n) via Maclaurin expansion + substitution
note: Berndt: "If two functions of x be equal, then a general theorem can be formed by simply writing phi(n) instead of x^n in the original theorem." THIS IS THE PROTO-MASTER-THEOREM move: replace x^n by phi(n) in any identity. The illustrative example tan^{-1} x + tan^{-1}(1/x) = pi/2 -> sum (-1)^n (phi(2n+1) + phi(-2n-1))/(2n+1) = (pi/2) phi(1) IS the Master-Theorem-style coefficient-extraction move. Although the modern Master-Theorem form (with Gamma(s) phi(-s)) doesn't fire until Entry 11, this framework section IS the pre-form. Tagging master_theorem because Berndt explicitly: 'In the introductory chapter of his book [20, p. 15] on the work of Ramanujan, Hardy quotes Corollary 1 [of E11] and remarks that this particularly interesting formula was one of Ramanujan's favorite formulas.' The §9 framework is the precursor.

note: Berndt: 'Ramanujan deduced this value by letting phi(z) = Gamma(z+1) and r = n in the Corollary [of E10].' This IS the Master Theorem applied to the Gamma function. Inherits.

note: Berndt: 'Ramanujan evidently put phi(z) = Gamma(z) sin(pi z / 2) in Example 1 to achieve the value of f(0).' Inherits master_theorem.

Same form as the QR I version tagged in diary 20. Canonical master_theorem firing.
